review_candidates.description: Organizational Context The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian ‎network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience ‎and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally ‎led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and ‎environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental ‎principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our ‎work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of ‎strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. ‎ IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the ‎Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, ‎service centres and delegations across the globe.‎ The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and ‎Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, ‎abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also ‎adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. ‎ Effective programme delivery therefore depends on strong integration between programme planning and financial ‎management. Programme teams need timely visibility of available funding, expenditure, commitments, forecasts, partner ‎transfers and donor conditions so that resources can be used for their intended purpose within agreed timeframes. The ‎Programme Finance and Grants Coordinator is positioned within Programme and Operations and works in close functional ‎collaboration with the Finance team to strengthen this link across the full project and grant management cycle.‎ The Administration Officer / Translator reports to the Administration Coordinator and provides administrative and translation/interpretation support to the Ukraine Operation. The role is approximately 70% administration and 30% operational translation and interpretation. Job Purpose Under the supervision of the Administration Coordinator, the Administration Officer / Translator provides high-quality administrative, travel, logistics and coordination support to the Ukraine Operation. Approximately 70% of the role is dedicated to administration, while 30% focuses on translation and interpretation support. The translation and interpretation component is primarily operational and field-oriented, including accompanying field trips and providing consecutive or simultaneous interpretation during operational visits, in-person meetings, trainings, events and other offline activities. Document translation and proofreading may be required as needed. Job Duties And Responsibilities Administration, Travel, Visa and Operational Support – approximately 70% Travel / Visa Management To carry out and coordinate travel arrangements, including air travel, transportation, hotel accommodation and insurance for delegates, staff and visitors, as required. Facilitate visa applications and extensions for travellers entering Ukraine, including preparation of supporting letters and coordination with relevant authorities and embassies. Notify hotels, travel agencies and other relevant suppliers promptly of any cancellations or changes and ensure confirmation of the notification. Support the organization of workshops, meetings, seminars and other events, including coordination of travel, accommodation, transportation and venue arrangements, procurement of required items, and other logistical support, in liaison with the Admin Coordinator and relevant colleagues, and negotiate favourable rates where appropriate. Maintain and update relevant travel and movement information in internal tracking systems and shared platforms, in liaison with Fleet / Security and relevant colleagues. Office Administration, Logistics Support Provide day-to-day office administration and logistical support, including procurement of office materials, equipment and stationery, errands and hospitality arrangements, ensuring a guest-friendly office environment. Manage office supplies and maintain adequate stock levels, promoting efficient use of resources and minimising waste. Collect GRN/SRN documents from suppliers, arrange stamping and returning the documents to vendors. Support the Admin Officer and relevant colleagues with key duplication, ID/business card printing, updating the movement board and other routine administrative tasks. Coordinate and monitor payments to external service providers and contracted suppliers in liaison with the Finance Unit, follow up on outstanding payments to avoid service disruption, and ensure proper cost coding for travel requests and other relevant expenses.
